source_refs.note: Exercise 4.3, Question 10: book page 77 (PDF 82); answer key PDF 303

blocks.prompt: 10 Use the matrix \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\) to encode the message: KEEP IT UP, where letters \(A\) to \(Z\) are corresponding to the numbers 1 to 26.
blocks.explanation:
An encoding question (cryptography), like Example 17 but with a \(3 \times 3\) matrix.
We must find the coded columns.
Plan: letters to numbers, groups of three (fill the last group), multiply each column by \(A\), check by decoding.
steps:
Given: \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\), message KEEP IT UP, A to Z = 1 to 26.
To find: the coded message.
Method: As in Example 17, change letters to numbers, cut them into groups of 3 (because \(A\) is \(3 \times 3\)), write each group as a \(3 \times 1\) column and multiply it on the left by \(A\).

Letters to numbers and groups of three
K = 11, E = 5, E = 5, P = 16, I = 9, T = 20, U = 21, P = 16.
Groups: KEE, PIT, UP. The last group has only two letters, so we fill it with 0.
\[\begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 5 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ 9 \\ 20\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}21 \\ 16 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\]
Why: A \(3 \times 3\) matrix can only multiply a \(3 \times 1\) column. Spaces between words are not coded. 0 stands for no letter (a blank), as the answer key does.

Encode KEE
\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 5 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}\]
\[1(11) + 0(5) + 1(5) = 16\]
\[2(11) + (-1)(5) + 1(5) = 22\]
\[0(11) + 1(5) + 2(5) = 15\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}16 \\ 22 \\ 15\end{bmatrix}\]
Why: Each entry is one row of \(A\) times the column.

Encode PIT
\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ 9 \\ 20\end{bmatrix}\]
\[1(16) + 0(9) + 1(20) = 36\]
\[2(16) + (-1)(9) + 1(20) = 43\]
\[0(16) + 1(9) + 2(20) = 49\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}36 \\ 43 \\ 49\end{bmatrix}\]
Why: Each entry is one row of \(A\) times the column.

Encode UP
\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}21 \\ 16 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\]
\[1(21) + 0(16) + 1(0) = 21\]
\[2(21) + (-1)(16) + 1(0) = 26\]
\[0(21) + 1(16) + 2(0) = 16\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}21 \\ 26 \\ 16\end{bmatrix}\]
Why: Each entry is one row of \(A\) times the column.

Check by decoding one group
With \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{-1}\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 1 & 1 \\ -4 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -1\end{bmatrix}\) (since \(|A| = -1\)):
\[A^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ 22 \\ 15\end{bmatrix} = \dfrac{1}{-1}\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ -5 \\ -5\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 5 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}\]
Why: Decoding must give back the numbers of KEE.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: KEEP IT UP has 8 letters, so the last group of three (UP) is one short. The question does not say how to fill it; the answer key's last column \([21, 26, 16]\) comes from using 0 for the empty place. With that convention the key \([16, 22, 15]\), \([36, 43, 49]\), \([21, 26, 16]\) is correct.
